title: Finite refinements give the hypercover-colimit relation
statement: For a qcqs scheme X, Grothendieck abelian A, sheaf F, finite split hypercovers U,V, q≥0 and a map t:trunc_(q+1)(U)→trunc_(q+1)(V), the induced map H^q(V,F)→H^q(U,F), followed by the U injection into hypercover cohomology, equals the V injection.

source.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 2: finite skeleton descent and finite-cochain section continuity; explicit categorical construction with Grothendieck coefficients.

proof.text: The finite coface construction gives a three-term map and respects composition by componentwise functoriality. For a full refinement its homology map is definitionally the usual cohomology refinement. Extend t using W,a,b,e with trunc(a)=e and trunc(b)=e followed by t. Composition of the finite maps identifies b on cohomology with t followed by a. Both full refinements satisfy the colimit injection relation, so substitution gives the claimed equation. Invertibility of the finite map is unnecessary.

mathlib_searches.query: Homology functor on short complexes preserves filtered colimits in a Grothendieck abelian category
The cohomology of a cosimplicial object in an abelian category depends only on its truncation through degree q plus one and maps of such truncations extend after hypercover refinement

theorem finiteRefinement_homology_comp_ι (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A)
    (U V : FiniteSplitEtaleHypercover X) (q : ℕ)
    (t : (SimplicialObject.truncation (q + 1)).obj U.simplicial ⟶
      (SimplicialObject.truncation (q + 1)).obj V.simplicial) :
    ShortComplex.homologyMap (finiteRefinementShortComplexMap A F q t) ≫
        hypercoverCohomologyι A F q U = hypercoverCohomologyι A F q V
